title: Keep the current random-key sorter target after the fixed-budget screen
question: Does three eighths of a 512 MiB job budget avoid the Uniform sorter spill for the synthetic Balanced consumer?
summary: Both builds spill twice. Median wall time is 0.927 seconds at the quarter target and 0.952 seconds at three eighths. Peak tracked reservations rise by about 62 MiB.

workloads: 524,291 synthetic rows, plain Uniform Shuffle followed by Balanced(8), 512 MiB, one worker, WSL2 ext4.

validation.summary: Three matched measured pairs and both warmups pass independent field and row conservation, exact quotas, lineage, manifest, byte and row caps, and workspace cleanup.

limitations: Neither arm reached resident execution. The initial runner invalidation is recorded separately and excluded from these samples.
One synthetic shape on one WSL host with uncontrolled warm cache. Random runs are independently verified and use distinct permutations.
exclusions: Fisher–Yates, browser, native Windows, physical-device I/O and lower-headroom and competing-owner safety.
reopen_when: Derive a plausible in-budget resident boundary from retained rows and overlap, then test matched jobs with meaningful absolute elapsed benefit and separate admission controls.
